It converts the packet into an unencrypted HTTP request
It permanently disables the ingress physical switch port
questions.explanation: When a rule action is 'Deny', matching packets are discarded by the firewall. Depending on configuration, the firewall may silently drop the packet or generate an active reset (TCP RST) or ICMP unreachable notification.

questions.stem: What is the valid priority range for creating custom user-defined security zones on a Huawei firewall?
options: 1 to 100 (excluding priorities already assigned to active zones)
Only priorities 10, 20, 30, and 40
questions.explanation: Custom security zones can be configured with priority values between 1 and 100. By default, priorities cannot overlap with existing zones (e.g., default priorities 5, 50, 85, 100 are already reserved).

questions.stem: Why is it best practice to place specific, high-frequency rules near the top of the security policy list?
options: To prevent the firewall's flash storage from fragmenting
Because top-down matching stops upon the first match; placing high-volume rules early minimizes CPU processing and matching latency
Because lower rules are permanently ignored after 5:00 PM
To automatically encrypt all low-priority traffic
questions.explanation: Since firewalls evaluate rules sequentially, placing rules for frequent traffic near the top reduces the number of rule comparisons the CPU must perform before finding a match, optimizing forwarding throughput.

questions.stem: Which Huawei VRP CLI command displays the active session table on a USG series firewall?
options: display current-configuration
display firewall session table
display ip routing-table
display mac-address
questions.explanation: The command `display firewall session table` displays active connection states, 5-tuples, zones, and timers currently tracked by the firewall.

questions.stem: What additional information is displayed when executing `display firewall session table verbose` on a Huawei firewall?
options: The physical MAC address of the firewall manufacturer
Detailed session attributes including ingress/egress interfaces, zone IDs, application IDs, packet/byte counters, and NAT translation details
The cleartext passwords of all domain administrators
The internal CPU register assembly code
questions.explanation: The `verbose` keyword expands the session display to show detailed flow parameters: application identification, NAT translations, input/output interface, TTL/aging timers, zone mappings, and packet/byte counters.

questions.stem: Why is stateful inspection superior to simple packet filtering in defending against external network scans?
options: Stateful inspection automatically doubles the link bandwidth
It permits return traffic only if it matches an existing session initiated from the inside, blocking unsolicited external packets without broad inbound port openings
It translates all external IP addresses into private addresses
It replaces all external routers with optical splitters
questions.explanation: Because stateful firewalls track connection states, return traffic for an internally initiated connection is automatically permitted via the session table. Inbound unsolicited connection attempts from the outside are dropped unless explicitly permitted by policy.

questions.stem: When an internal client accesses an external FTP server, the initial control session is established to which destination port?
options: TCP port 20
TCP port 21
UDP port 69
TCP port 22
questions.explanation: FTP control commands (USER, PASS, PORT, PASV) are transmitted over TCP port 21. Data connections use port 20 (Active mode) or negotiated dynamic ports (Passive mode).

questions.stem: What is the function of associating a 'Time Range' (schedule) with a firewall security policy rule?
options: To automatically change the firewall's system clock
To activate the security policy rule only during specified dates, days of the week, or hours of the day
To measure the round-trip latency of user packets
To limit user connection durations to exactly 15 seconds
questions.explanation: A Time Range schedule allows administrators to restrict the validity of a security rule to specific working hours, weekdays, or promotional periods, automatically deactivating the rule outside the designated window.

questions.stem: What is the administrative benefit of defining an 'Address Set' object and referencing it within security policies?
options: It allows multiple IP addresses or subnets to be managed collectively, simplifying policy rules and ongoing maintenance
It eliminates the need for subnet masks across all enterprise servers
It forces all referenced IP addresses to use identical MAC addresses
It converts private IP addresses directly into public DNS domain names
questions.explanation: Address Sets group multiple IP addresses, ranges, or subnets into a single logical object. When IP addresses change, updating the object automatically updates all associated security policies without modifying individual rules.

questions.stem: What information is encapsulated within a custom 'Service Object' on a Huawei firewall?
options: The physical location and room number of a server
Transport protocol (TCP/UDP/ICMP) and source/destination port ranges
The monthly billing cost of an enterprise application
The firmware revision of connected switches
questions.explanation: A Service Object defines network protocols and port parameters (e.g., protocol TCP, destination port 8080-8088), allowing custom enterprise applications to be referenced cleanly in security policies.

questions.stem: How does Huawei NGFW Service Awareness (SA) identify network applications regardless of the port number used?
options: By reading the destination port number only
Through deep packet inspection (DPI) analyzing application-layer packet payload signatures and behavioral features
By contacting the software developer over the telephone
By randomly assigning application names based on IP addresses
questions.explanation: Huawei NGFW employs Deep Packet Inspection (DPI) and behavioral heuristics to inspect application-layer payloads and protocol handshakes, accurately identifying applications (e.g., BitTorrent, WeChat, Facebook) even when they run over non-standard ports or port 80/443.

questions.stem: Why would an administrator enable the 'traffic statistics' (counter) feature on a security policy rule?
options: To calculate employee salaries based on bandwidth usage
To verify if the policy rule is actually matching traffic and monitor the volume of permitted/denied packets and bytes
To permanently store all transmitted files in the cloud
To disable the rule automatically when traffic reaches 100 megabytes
questions.explanation: Policy counters track the number of matching packets and bytes. This is crucial for verifying policy effectiveness, troubleshooting rule ordering issues, and identifying unused legacy rules for decommissioning.

questions.stem: How does a firewall regulate administrative access (HTTPS, SSH, Ping) to its own physical interfaces?
options: Management traffic to the firewall interface terminates in the Local zone and is controlled via interface access management or Local zone security policies
Management access is permitted automatically on all interfaces without restriction
Management traffic cannot be processed by firewalls
By disabling all IP routing on management ports
questions.explanation: Interface management services (Ping, SSH, HTTPS, NETCONF) are governed by interface access management settings and security policies between the originating zone (e.g., Trust) and the Local zone (priority 100).

questions.stem: If an administrator desires to block communication between two departments whose interfaces reside in the same Trust zone, what must be done?
options: The firewall hardware must be replaced with two physical firewalls
An intra-zone security policy with the action 'Deny' must be configured, or intra-zone inter-interface filtering must be enabled
Intra-zone traffic can never be blocked under any circumstances
All departmental PCs must be powered off
questions.explanation: Although intra-zone traffic is permitted by default, administrators can enforce security by creating explicit intra-zone security policies (Source Zone: Trust, Destination Zone: Trust) with 'Deny' actions or enabling intra-zone packet filtering.

questions.stem: What issue arises when asymmetric routing causes outbound packets to traverse Firewall A but return packets to traverse Firewall B?
options: Firewall B drops the return packets because it lacks an existing session table entry for the connection
Firewall A immediately powers off its cooling fans
The client's network interface card is permanently damaged
The destination server sends duplicate SYN packets indefinitely
questions.explanation: In asymmetric routing, Firewall B receives return packets without having seen the initial SYN packet that creates the session. Because stateful detection is enabled, Firewall B drops the unsolicited return packet as an invalid state transition unless session synchronization or stateful inspection exceptions are configured.

questions.stem: What happens when a firewall's session table reaches its maximum hardware capacity during a severe connection flood?
options: The firewall begins formatting its hard drives
New connection requests cannot be established and are discarded, resulting in denial of service for new users
The firewall converts all TCP traffic into unencrypted UDP broadcasts
Existing established sessions are immediately deleted
questions.explanation: The session table has a finite maximum capacity dictated by available memory. When full, the firewall cannot allocate new session entries, causing all subsequent new connection requests to be dropped.

questions.stem: If stateful inspection is globally disabled on a firewall interface, how does the firewall behave?
options: It functions like a stateless packet filter, requiring explicit policy rules for both forward and return traffic flows
It permanently blocks 100% of all IP traffic
It automatically encrypts all traffic using IPsec
It forwards all packets exclusively to the DMZ zone
questions.explanation: When stateful inspection is disabled, the firewall stops creating session tables. It evaluates every single packet in isolation like a traditional stateless packet filter, requiring administrators to write explicit rules for both forward request and return response traffic.

questions.stem: In Huawei NGFWs, which security features are attached to a permitted security policy rule as 'Security Profiles'?
options: Antivirus, IPS, URL Filtering, File Filtering, Content Filtering, and Mail Filtering
BGP, OSPF, RIP, and IS-IS routing tables
DHCP Server address pool ranges and lease timers
Interface physical duplex and speed settings
questions.explanation: Security Profiles (IPS, Antivirus, URL Filtering, File/Content Filtering, Application Control) are bound to 'Permit' security policy rules to perform deep Layer 7 content inspection on traffic that passes basic 5-tuple filtering.

questions.stem: Why is it recommended to enable session logging only on specific critical policies rather than logging every single permitted packet in high-throughput environments?
options: Because logging is prohibited by international networking RFCs
To avoid exhausting firewall CPU, disk I/O, and log server storage caused by billions of routine session logs
Because session logs contain unencrypted passwords
To prevent the firewall from generating IP routing updates
questions.explanation: Generating logs for every permitted connection in a multi-gigabit data center creates massive CPU overhead and storage exhaustion. Best practice is to log denied traffic, threat alerts, and critical business policies.

questions.stem: What was the primary initial driver for the invention and widespread adoption of Network Address Translation (NAT)?
options: To increase the physical clock speed of network switches
To mitigate the rapid exhaustion of the public IPv4 address space
To eliminate the need for routing tables in wide area networks
To encrypt all web traffic using SSL/TLS
questions.explanation: The rapid depletion of the 32-bit IPv4 address space was the primary catalyst for NAT, enabling multiple private internal hosts to share one or a few public IP addresses for Internet access.

questions.stem: In which type of Source NAT is only the private IP address translated to a public IP address from a pool, WITHOUT translating transport layer port numbers?
options: NAPT
NAT No-PAT
Easy IP
Smart NAT
questions.explanation: NAT No-PAT (No Port Address Translation) performs 1-to-1 IP address translation without modifying source port numbers. The number of concurrent external connections is strictly limited to the number of public IPs in the address pool.

questions.stem: If an enterprise configures a NAT No-PAT address pool containing 5 public IPv4 addresses, how many internal hosts can concurrently access the Internet simultaneously?
options: 5 hosts
500 hosts
65,535 hosts
Unlimited hosts
questions.explanation: Because NAT No-PAT does not multiplex sessions using transport layer port numbers, each concurrent internal host requires a dedicated public IP address. Thus, 5 public IPs can support at most 5 concurrent hosts.

questions.stem: Which Source NAT technology translates both the private IP address and the source port number into a public IP address and a unique public port number?
options: NAT No-PAT
NAPT (Network Address Port Translation)
NAT Server
Static 1-to-1 NAT
questions.explanation: NAPT translates both source IP addresses and source port numbers. By mapping internal sockets (IP:Port) to public sockets, thousands of internal hosts can simultaneously share a single public IP address.

questions.stem: What is the defining characteristic of the Easy IP translation technology in Huawei firewalls?
options: It requires a pre-allocated pool of at least 16 public IP addresses
It directly utilizes the public IP address configured on the firewall's egress interface for translation, eliminating the need for an address pool
It translates destination IP addresses exclusively for database servers
It disables stateful session table creation
questions.explanation: Easy IP is a specialized form of NAPT that uses the public IP address dynamically or statically assigned to the firewall's egress interface. It requires no address pool configuration, making it ideal for PPPoE dial-up or DHCP WAN connections.

questions.stem: For which network environment is Easy IP predominantly recommended?
options: Data centers hosting 500 public-facing web servers
Small office / home office (SOHO) or enterprise branch locations with dynamic WAN IP addresses obtained via PPPoE or DHCP
Internal corporate subnets communicating with isolated DMZ servers
Core ISP backbones routing BGP full tables
questions.explanation: Because SOHO and branch networks frequently obtain dynamic, changing public IP addresses from ISPs via DHCP or PPPoE, Easy IP automatically tracks the interface IP without requiring static address pool adjustments.

questions.stem: How does Smart NAT operate on a Huawei firewall when the public IP address pool is under heavy load?
options: It drops all new incoming and outgoing packets immediately
It initially performs 1-to-1 No-PAT translation; when pool addresses are exhausted, it uses a reserved public IP to perform NAPT for remaining hosts
It reboots the firewall into recovery mode
It converts all TCP sessions into unencrypted UDP broadcasts
questions.explanation: Smart NAT combines No-PAT and NAPT. High-priority or initial users receive dedicated 1-to-1 No-PAT translations from the pool. When available IPs run out, a designated reserved IP in the pool performs NAPT for all remaining hosts.

questions.stem: What is the primary function of the 'NAT Server' feature on a Huawei firewall?
options: To translate internal client source IPs when browsing external websites
To statically map a public IP address and port to an internal server's private IP address and port, allowing Internet users to access intranet servers
To provide automatic DHCP address leases to local PCs
To act as an authoritative DNS root nameserver
questions.explanation: NAT Server (Destination NAT with port mapping) publishes intranet servers to the Internet. It maps public IP:Port combinations to private server IP:Port combinations, enabling external users to reach internal web, mail, or FTP servers.

questions.stem: Which forwarding table entry is automatically created when a 'NAT Server' rule is configured on a Huawei firewall?
options: A dynamic ARP table entry
A static Server-Map table entry
A BGP routing table entry
An OSPF link-state advertisement
questions.explanation: Configuring a `nat server` rule automatically creates a permanent, static Server-Map table entry that stores the mapping between the public IP/port and private IP/port.

questions.stem: Which NAT technique simultaneously translates BOTH the source IP address and destination IP address of the same packet?
options: NAT No-PAT
Easy IP
Bidirectional NAT
NAT ALG
questions.explanation: Bidirectional NAT performs Source NAT and Destination NAT concurrently on a single packet flow. It is essential when internal hosts access internal servers using the server's public IP (NAT hairpinning) or to prevent asymmetric routing.

questions.stem: When an intranet client attempts to access an intranet server using the server's public IP address without Bidirectional NAT, why does the connection fail?
options: The server replies directly to the client's private IP, causing the client to discard the response due to socket address mismatch
The firewall physically powers off its egress interface
The DNS server refuses to resolve domain names ending in .com
The Ethernet frame size exceeds 9000 bytes
questions.explanation: When Destination NAT translates the public IP to the server's private IP, the server receives a packet with the client's private source IP. The server replies directly via the local switch to the client's private IP. The client, expecting a reply from the public IP, drops the packet because the source socket does not match.

questions.stem: How does Bidirectional NAT resolve the NAT hairpinning problem for intranet clients accessing intranet servers via public IP?
options: It translates the destination IP to the server's private IP AND translates the client's source IP to a firewall interface IP
It forces all traffic to route across the public Internet to the ISP before returning
It disables TCP checksum validation on the server
It converts all HTTP requests to FTP downloads
questions.explanation: By applying Destination NAT (public server IP -> private server IP) and Source NAT (client private IP -> firewall IP), the server replies back to the firewall. The firewall reverses both translations and sends the reply to the client from the expected public IP.

questions.stem: Why is standard NAT incapable of successfully translating multi-channel protocols like FTP active mode without an Application Level Gateway (ALG)?
options: FTP packets are encrypted using 4096-bit RSA keys
Standard NAT translates only IP/port headers; it cannot inspect or modify IP addresses and port numbers embedded inside the application-layer payload (e.g. PORT commands)
FTP cannot operate over IPv4 networks
Standard NAT automatically deletes all files being transferred
questions.explanation: Standard NAT rewrites Layer 3 IP headers and Layer 4 TCP/UDP headers. In FTP active mode, the client transmits its private IP and data port as text inside the application-layer payload (`PORT h1,h2,h3,h4,p1,p2`). Without ALG, the server attempts to connect to the unreachable private IP.

questions.stem: What actions does a NAT ALG perform when inspecting an FTP active mode control connection?
options: It translates the private IP and port embedded inside the application payload to the public IP/port AND creates a dynamic Server-Map entry for the data connection
It blocks the connection and alerts the domain administrator
It converts the FTP transfer into an email attachment
It forces the client to use Telnet instead
questions.explanation: NAT ALG parses the application payload, rewrites the embedded IP/port string to the corresponding public IP/port, and generates a dynamic Server-Map entry to allow the server's incoming data connection through the firewall.

questions.stem: What is the primary technical reason for configuring a NAT Blackhole Route (`ip route-static <pool-ip> 32 NULL0`) on a Huawei firewall?
options: To prevent routing loops between the firewall and upstream ISP gateway when packets arrive for unused addresses in the NAT pool
To permanently delete all infected malware files
To prevent internal users from accessing social media websites
To test the maximum bandwidth throughput of the firewall backplane
questions.explanation: If public address pool IPs are not assigned to the firewall interface, an incoming packet destined to an idle pool IP is bounced between the upstream ISP router (which routes the pool to the firewall) and the firewall (which has a default route back to the ISP), creating an infinite routing loop. A blackhole route drops the packet immediately.

questions.stem: Which Huawei VRP CLI command creates an address pool for Source NAT?
options: nat address-group <group-number> <start-ip> <end-ip>
ip pool <name>
dhcp server ip-pool
firewall nat-pool create
questions.explanation: In Huawei firewalls, the command `nat address-group <group-id> <start-ip> <end-ip>` (or in newer USG models `nat address-group <name>`) defines the pool of public IPv4 addresses available for translation.

questions.stem: In what order are rules evaluated within a Huawei firewall's NAT Policy rulebase?
options: Alphabetical order by rule name
Top-to-bottom sequential matching; the first matching rule is executed and matching terminates
Bottom-to-top reverse matching
Random selection based on CPU load
questions.explanation: Similar to security policies, NAT policies are evaluated sequentially from top to bottom. Once a packet matches a NAT rule's conditions, the translation action is executed and evaluation stops.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of configuring a NAT policy rule with the action 'no-nat' on a Huawei firewall?
options: To disable the firewall's routing engine
To exempt specific traffic (such as branch-to-branch IPsec VPN traffic) from undergoing NAT translation
To format the firewall's solid-state drive
To force all traffic to be logged in cleartext
questions.explanation: When an enterprise establishes an IPsec tunnel between branches, traffic between internal private subnets must not be translated to public IPs. A high-priority 'no-nat' rule exempts VPN traffic from standard Internet Source NAT.

questions.stem: How does general Destination NAT differ from NAT Server in Huawei firewall configuration?
options: NAT Server statically maps specific public ports to specific private servers, whereas general Destination NAT translates destination IPs to a pool of addresses (often with port preservation or load balancing)
Destination NAT only works for IPv6 packets
NAT Server works only when the firewall is powered off
There is no difference; they are exact synonyms
questions.explanation: NAT Server provides 1-to-1 static port and IP mapping for publishing internal servers. General Destination NAT maps traffic destined for public IPs to an internal address pool, commonly utilized for server farm load balancing.

questions.stem: Approximately how many concurrent translation sessions can theoretically be supported per public IPv4 address in NAPT?
options: Only 1 session
Approximately 60,000 to 64,000 concurrent sessions (bounded by 16-bit transport port range)
Exactly 256 sessions
Unlimited sessions without memory usage
questions.explanation: Transport layer source ports are 16-bit integers (ports 1024 to 65535, minus reserved ports), allowing roughly 60,000 concurrent translated flows per transport protocol per public IP address.

questions.stem: In NAT No-PAT, when is a public IP address released back to the address pool for another internal host to use?
options: Never; once assigned, it is permanently locked to that host MAC
When all session table entries for that internal host expire or age out
Every 60 seconds regardless of active traffic
Only when the firewall is manually rebooted
questions.explanation: In No-PAT, a public IP is allocated to an internal host and mapped in the Server-Map table. When all active connection sessions for that host terminate and the Server-Map aging timer expires, the public IP returns to the free pool.

questions.stem: Why would an enterprise deploy NAT Multipool configuration on a border firewall?
options: To map different internal departments or user groups to distinct public IP address pools for traffic separation, auditing, and QoS
To allow internal users to share identical MAC addresses
To replace BGP routing across multiple ISPs
To convert copper Ethernet interfaces into optical ports
questions.explanation: NAT Multipool allows an enterprise to direct traffic from different departments, guest Wi-Fi networks, or business units to separate public IP address pools, enabling granular billing, ISP policy routing, and security isolation.

questions.stem: Which command displays the active NAT translation mappings and session details on a Huawei USG firewall?
options: display firewall session table verbose
display ip interface brief
display version
display device
questions.explanation: Executing `display firewall session table verbose` displays detailed session records, including the original 5-tuple and the translated NAT 5-tuple (`-->` translation indicators).

questions.stem: In Huawei VRP CLI, which command correctly configures a static NAT Server rule publishing an internal web server?
options: nat server protocol tcp global 203.0.113.10 80 inside 192.168.1.100 80
firewall web publish 203.0.113.10 to 192.168.1.100
questions.explanation: The standard Huawei VRP command syntax is: `nat server [zone <zone>] protocol tcp global <public-ip> <public-port> inside <private-ip> <private-port>`.

questions.topic: NAT ALG Enabled Protocols by Default
questions.stem: On many Huawei firewalls, for which protocol is NAT ALG typically enabled by default due to its widespread operational necessity?
options: FTP
BGP
RIP
OSPF
questions.explanation: FTP is the classic multi-channel protocol with ubiquitous enterprise usage; firewalls commonly have FTP ALG enabled by default (`firewall detect ftp`).

questions.topic: Source IP vs Destination IP Translation
questions.stem: When an internal host (192.168.1.10) browses an external website (93.184.216.34) through Source NAT (public IP 203.0.113.5), what does the packet header look like as it leaves the firewall's egress interface?
options: Source IP: 192.168.1.10, Destination IP: 203.0.113.5
Source IP: 203.0.113.5, Destination IP: 93.184.216.34
Source IP: 93.184.216.34, Destination IP: 192.168.1.10
Source IP: 203.0.113.5, Destination IP: 192.168.1.10
questions.explanation: Source NAT replaces the private source IP (192.168.1.10) with the public IP (203.0.113.5). The destination IP remains the external web server's IP (93.184.216.34).

questions.stem: When an external client (198.51.100.25) accesses an internal web server published via NAT Server (public IP 203.0.113.10 -> private IP 192.168.1.100), what does the packet header look like after leaving the firewall towards the server?
options: Source IP: 198.51.100.25, Destination IP: 192.168.1.100
Source IP: 203.0.113.10, Destination IP: 192.168.1.100
Source IP: 192.168.1.100, Destination IP: 198.51.100.25
Source IP: 198.51.100.25, Destination IP: 203.0.113.10
questions.explanation: NAT Server performs Destination NAT: the destination IP is translated from the public address (203.0.113.10) to the internal private address (192.168.1.100). The original client source IP (198.51.100.25) is preserved.

questions.stem: In Bidirectional NAT, after translation by the firewall, what happens to both Source and Destination IP fields?
options: Neither field is modified
Both the Source IP and Destination IP addresses are rewritten to new values
Only the TCP checksum is recalculated without IP changes
The packet is converted to an unroutable broadcast frame
questions.explanation: In Bidirectional NAT, the firewall translates the Source IP (e.g., from client private IP to firewall interface IP) AND translates the Destination IP (from public server IP to private server IP) simultaneously.

questions.stem: Why does NAT No-PAT generate a Server-Map entry upon the first packet translation?
options: To track the 1-to-1 mapping between the private host IP and assigned public pool IP, ensuring subsequent inbound or outbound packets from that host use the same public IP
To permanently disable all firewall security policies for that host
To record the user's keystrokes for forensic logging
To translate the host's operating system language
questions.explanation: NAT No-PAT creates a dynamic Server-Map entry binding the host's private IP to the allocated public IP. This ensures all concurrent flows from that host share the identical public IP and permits incoming sessions if configured.

questions.topic: NAT Policy vs Security Policy Processing Order
questions.stem: On a Huawei firewall processing an OUTBOUND packet from Trust to Untrust with Source NAT, what is the correct processing order between Security Policy and NAT Policy?
options: The packet is translated by NAT Policy first, and then matches Security Policy based on the translated public IP
The packet matches Security Policy first based on its original private IP; if permitted, it is then processed by NAT Policy for source translation
Security Policy and NAT Policy are evaluated by separate physical processors at the same time
NAT Policy is evaluated only after the packet reaches the destination web server
questions.explanation: On outbound flows, the firewall first checks Security Policy against the original private source IP and destination IP. If traffic is permitted, the packet enters the NAT pipeline where Source NAT translates the source IP address.

questions.stem: When an external Internet user accesses an internal server published via NAT Server, what is the processing order between Destination NAT and Security Policy?
options: Security Policy is evaluated using the public IP; destination translation never occurs
Destination NAT translation occurs first (or server-map matches), and the Security Policy is evaluated using the translated private IP address
Security Policy is bypassed completely for all inbound traffic
The packet is held in storage for 24 hours before inspection
questions.explanation: For inbound traffic targeting a NAT Server, destination translation (Server-Map matching) occurs before security policy evaluation. Therefore, the security policy rule permitting inbound traffic must specify the internal private IP address of the server as the destination!

questions.stem: What impact does running heavy NAPT translation have on a firewall's hardware resources?
options: It has zero impact because translation is done on the client NIC
It consumes CPU cycles for port allocation/checksum recalculation and memory for maintaining stateful session and NAT mapping tables
It permanently damages the optical fiber transceivers
It reduces the physical storage capacity of the hard drive
questions.explanation: NAPT requires tracking port states, rewriting IP/TCP/UDP headers, recalculating checksums, and managing session memory, imposing higher compute and memory overhead than stateless routing.

questions.stem: Why is the IPsec Authentication Header (AH) protocol fundamentally incompatible with NAT?
options: AH uses 56-bit DES encryption
AH calculates its cryptographic integrity check value (ICV) over the entire IP packet including the outer IP header; NAT alters IP addresses, causing AH integrity verification to fail
AH operates only over dial-up telephone lines
AH packets cannot be routed across Ethernet switches
questions.explanation: AH provides data integrity by hashing the entire packet, including IP source and destination addresses. When NAT translates an IP address, the receiver's computed hash fails to match the transmitted ICV, causing the packet to be dropped.

questions.stem: How does NAT Traversal (NAT-T) resolve the problem of passing IPsec ESP traffic through a NAT router/firewall?
options: By converting the entire packet into cleartext HTTP
By encapsulating the IPsec ESP packet inside a UDP header using port 4500, allowing NAT devices to translate ports normally
By disabling encryption on the IPsec tunnel
By forcing the NAT router to adopt an IPv6 address
questions.explanation: Because standard ESP lacks transport layer ports, NAPT devices cannot translate multiple ESP streams. NAT-T encapsulates ESP packets inside UDP datagrams using port 4500, enabling standard NAPT port translation and preserving encryption integrity.

questions.topic: NAT Address Group Mode - No-PAT Keyword
questions.stem: In Huawei VRP CLI, which keyword is appended to the address group configuration to enforce 1-to-1 translation without port multiplexing?
options: pat
no-pat
easy-ip
smart
questions.explanation: In Huawei firewall configuration, the keyword `no-pat` (e.g., `section 0 203.0.113.10 203.0.113.20 no-pat`) specifies that the address pool operates in No-PAT mode.

questions.stem: What is the effect of configuring the `no-reverse` keyword in a Huawei `nat server` declaration?
options: It prevents the firewall from generating a reverse Server-Map entry, ensuring internal server outbound connections do not automatically use this public IP
It disables the server's network adapter
It blocks all inbound traffic to the server
It reverses the polarity of the Ethernet cable
questions.explanation: By default, `nat server` creates forward and reverse mappings. When the internal server initiates outbound connections, it is translated to the public server IP. The `no-reverse` keyword disables reverse translation, allowing outbound server traffic to match general Internet NAT policies.

questions.stem: What is the primary operational difference between Static NAT and Dynamic NAT?
options: Static NAT establishes a permanent, fixed 1-to-1 mapping between a private IP and public IP, whereas Dynamic NAT assigns public IPs dynamically from a pool on a first-come, first-served basis
Static NAT only works during daytime hours
Dynamic NAT requires unshielded twisted pair copper cabling
Static NAT disables firewall routing capabilities
questions.explanation: Static NAT maps a specific private IP to a specific public IP permanently. Dynamic NAT draws public IPs dynamically from an address pool when active traffic arrives, releasing them when connections expire.

questions.stem: Why is Bidirectional NAT commonly configured on the DMZ interface for internal users accessing intranet servers?
options: To ensure the internal server sends return packets back through the firewall rather than directly across the local switch to the client
To force all traffic to be logged by the ISP
To accelerate DNS resolution speed
To convert TCP packets into SCTP format
questions.explanation: Translating the client's source IP to a firewall interface IP forces the server to return packets to the firewall. The firewall untranslates both source and destination IPs, ensuring the client receives return packets matching its original public destination IP.

questions.stem: In industry terminology, what is 'Twice NAT' another name for?
options: Applying NAT twice in series across two separate firewalls
Bidirectional NAT (translating both source and destination addresses on the same device simultaneously)
Translating only the TCP sequence numbers
Formatting the firewall configuration twice
questions.explanation: Twice NAT is standard industry terminology for Bidirectional NAT, where an appliance rewrites both the source and destination IP addresses of a single packet flow.

questions.stem: Which command is used on a Huawei firewall to verify configured NAT address groups and their utilization?
options: display nat address-group
display ip pool
display current-nat
display memory nat
questions.explanation: The command `display nat address-group` displays configured NAT address pools, start/end IP addresses, assigned modes (PAT or No-PAT), and current IP allocation status.

questions.stem: Which of the following multimedia signaling protocols requires NAT ALG on firewalls to negotiate audio/video RTP streaming channels across NAT boundaries?
options: SIP (Session Initiation Protocol)
SNMP
NTP
Syslog
questions.explanation: SIP embeds private IP addresses and dynamic RTP media ports inside its Session Description Protocol (SDP) payload. A SIP ALG translates these embedded addresses and creates Server-Map pinholes for the voice/video media streams.

questions.stem: What happens if an administrator configures a NAT address pool with an IP range that overlaps with the IP assigned to an active interface on the firewall?
options: The firewall will produce a configuration error or warning because overlapping IP assignments cause ARP and routing conflicts
The firewall automatically doubles the interface speed to compensate
All firewall interfaces are permanently disabled
The firewall converts into a wireless access point
questions.explanation: Public address pool IPs must not conflict with interface IPs unless Easy IP is explicitly configured. Overlapping addresses cause IP conflicts and ARP broadcast anomalies.

questions.stem: In enterprise high availability (HA) network design, what availability percentage is commonly known as 'five nines' availability?
questions.explanation: 'Five nines' refers to 99.999% system availability, allowing at most approximately 5.26 minutes of unscheduled downtime per year across enterprise services.

questions.stem: Virtual Router Redundancy Protocol (VRRP) is standard protocol defined by which standards body?
options: IEEE 802.3
IETF (RFC 3768 / RFC 5798)
ITU-T X.509
questions.explanation: VRRP is an open industry standard protocol defined by the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) in RFC 3768 (VRRPv2) and RFC 5798 (VRRPv3) to provide gateway redundancy.

questions.stem: What is the standard format of a VRRP Virtual MAC address for an IPv4 VRRP group with VRID 1?
options: FF-FF-FF-FF-FF-01
questions.explanation: The standard VRRP IPv4 Virtual MAC format is `00-00-5E-00-01-XX`, where the last byte `XX` represents the VRID in hexadecimal. For VRID 1, the Virtual MAC is `00-00-5E-00-01-01`.

questions.stem: What is the default priority value assigned to a router participating in a standard VRRP group?
questions.explanation: The default VRRP priority is 100. Configurable priorities range from 1 to 254. Priority 255 is automatically reserved for the router that owns the actual physical IP address matching the Virtual IP.

questions.stem: By default, at what interval does the VRRP Master router broadcast VRRP Advertisement packets?
options: 100 milliseconds
1 second
5 seconds
30 seconds
questions.explanation: The default VRRP advertisement interval is 1 second. If the Backup router fails to receive advertisements for three consecutive intervals (3 * Advertisement_Interval + Skew_Time), it transitions to Master.

questions.stem: What is the standard IPv4 multicast address used by the VRRP Master to send advertisement packets to backup routers?
questions.explanation: VRRP protocol advertisements are encapsulated in IP packets (Protocol 112) and transmitted to the dedicated multicast address `224.0.0.18`.

questions.stem: What is the primary technical limitation of deploying standard standalone VRRP on multi-interface stateful firewalls?
options: VRRP cannot run over Ethernet interfaces
VRRP groups on uplink and downlink interfaces operate independently; a failure on the uplink does not trigger a failover on the downlink, creating a routing black hole
VRRP disables all NAT translation features on firewalls
VRRP requires physical serial cables between routers
questions.explanation: Standard VRRP operates per-interface independently. If Firewall A's external uplink fails, its internal interface remains VRRP Master. Internal traffic still flows to Firewall A, where it is blackholed because Firewall A has lost its upstream path.

questions.stem: What is the VRRP Group Management Protocol (VGMP) on Huawei firewalls?
options: An open IETF protocol used to configure wireless access points
A Huawei proprietary protocol that manages all VRRP groups on a firewall as a unified entity to coordinate synchronized state switchovers
A protocol used exclusively to update antivirus signature databases
A routing protocol replacing OSPF in data centers
questions.explanation: VGMP is a Huawei proprietary protocol that groups all VRRP interfaces (uplink, downlink, DMZ) under a centralized management group, ensuring that when one interface fails, all VRRP groups switch states together.

questions.stem: In Huawei firewall hot standby, what are the two predefined VGMP management groups?
options: Active Group and Standby Group
Master Group and Slave Group
Primary Group and Secondary Group
Trust Group and Untrust Group
questions.explanation: VGMP provides two management groups: the Active Group (default state is Active) and the Standby Group (default state is Standby).

questions.stem: What is the default initial priority of both the Active and Standby VGMP management groups on Huawei firewalls?
questions.explanation: By default, the initial priority of both the Active VGMP group and the Standby VGMP group is 65000.

questions.stem: When a monitored interface on the active firewall goes DOWN, how does VGMP adjust its group priority by default?
options: It resets the priority to 0
It decrements the VGMP priority (typically by 2) for each failed monitored interface
It doubles the VGMP priority to compensate
It leaves the priority unchanged and reboots the firewall
questions.explanation: When an interface tracked by VGMP fails, VGMP reduces its priority value (default reduction is 2). This causes the active firewall's priority (e.g. 64998) to drop below the standby firewall's priority (65000), triggering an immediate switchover.

questions.stem: What occurs across all VRRP groups on a firewall when its VGMP management group transitions from Active to Standby?
options: All associated VRRP groups switch from Master to Backup simultaneously
All internal network switches lose power
Only the failed interface switches, while others remain unchanged
The firewall formats its configuration disk
questions.explanation: Because VGMP centrally controls all member VRRP groups, when the VGMP group changes state, every associated VRRP group (internal, external, DMZ) transitions simultaneously, preventing asymmetric routing black holes.

questions.stem: What is the primary role of the Huawei Redundancy Protocol (HRP)?
options: To assign IP addresses to DHCP clients across the WAN
To synchronize configuration commands, session tables, and status information between active and standby firewalls over heartbeat interfaces
To provide public key digital certificate verification
To calculate shortest path trees for OSPF routing
questions.explanation: HRP is a Huawei proprietary protocol running over heartbeat links that synchronizes configuration commands (`hrp enable`), dynamic session tables, Server-Map entries, and IPsec SA states between clustered firewalls.

questions.stem: Which transport protocol and port number are utilized by HRP heartbeat packets?
options: TCP port 80
UDP port 18514
TCP port 443
UDP port 500
questions.explanation: HRP encapsulates heartbeat packets and synchronization data inside UDP datagrams using destination port 18514.

questions.stem: Which of the following dynamic state tables is synchronized in real-time by HRP to prevent active TCP sessions from dropping during a failover?
options: The BGP routing information base (RIB)
The firewall Session Table
The switch STP topology change table
The CPU instruction cache
questions.explanation: Real-time session table synchronization by HRP ensures that the backup firewall maintains an identical copy of active connection states. When a failover occurs, established TCP connections continue without interruption.

questions.stem: When does HRP 'Real-Time Backup' execute data synchronization?
options: Once every 24 hours at midnight
Immediately as each new session table entry or configuration command is created or modified
Only when the administrator manually enters a synchronization command
Only when an interface physically fails
questions.explanation: Real-time backup continuously replicates state changes: as soon as a new session is established or a security policy is modified, HRP immediately transmits the update to the standby peer.

questions.stem: Under which circumstance is HRP 'Batch Backup' primarily triggered?
options: During an active DDoS attack
When the standby firewall boots up, re-establishes heartbeat connectivity, or an administrator manually triggers `hrp sync config`
When a user types a wrong password three times
Whenever an ICMP ping packet is received
questions.explanation: Batch backup bulk-synchronizes all configuration commands and existing session tables. It executes upon initial peer connection establishment, manual administrator command (`hrp sync`), or after a reboot.

questions.stem: Why is 'Quick Session Backup' specifically implemented in Load-Balancing (Active/Active) hot standby mode?
options: To immediately replicate sessions before return packets arrive in asymmetric routing topologies, preventing session drop on the peer firewall
To permanently disable stateful packet inspection
To reduce CPU clock speeds during business hours
To convert TCP packets into UDP broadcasts
questions.explanation: In Active/Active mode, asymmetric routing can cause outbound traffic to traverse FW1 while return traffic reaches FW2. Quick session backup instantly pushes the session from FW1 to FW2 upon creation so FW2 can forward the return packet without dropping it.

questions.stem: In Active/Standby (1+1 Redundancy) mode, how is network traffic handled under normal operating conditions?
options: Both firewalls forward 50% of the traffic simultaneously
The Active firewall processes all service traffic, while the Standby firewall remains idle ready to take over upon failure
The Standby firewall processes only voice traffic
Traffic bypasses both firewalls completely
questions.explanation: In Active/Standby mode, one firewall (the active unit) handles all network forwarding, policy enforcement, and NAT. The standby firewall does not forward traffic; it synchronizes states and monitors the active unit.

questions.stem: In Load-Balancing (Active/Active) mode, how are VRRP groups typically deployed across the two firewalls?
options: Both firewalls are configured as Backup for all VRRP groups
Firewall A is configured as Master for VRRP Group 1 and Backup for Group 2; Firewall B is configured as Master for Group 2 and Backup for Group 1
Neither firewall is assigned a virtual IP address
VRRP is completely disabled on both firewalls
questions.explanation: In Active/Active mode, services are divided between two VRRP groups. FW1 is Master for Group 1 (gateway for Subnet A), and FW2 is Master for Group 2 (gateway for Subnet B). Both forward traffic concurrently, providing mutual backup.

questions.stem: What type of interface is recommended for connecting the HRP heartbeat link between two clustered firewalls?
options: A dedicated point-to-point Layer 3 physical interface or dedicated Eth-Trunk
A public Internet WAN interface routed through an external ISP
An unmanaged consumer Wi-Fi connection
An optical interface connected to an analog television tuner
questions.explanation: Best practice mandates dedicated point-to-point physical links (or aggregated Eth-Trunk links) directly connecting the two firewalls for heartbeat traffic, preventing heartbeat loss from intermediate switch failures.

questions.stem: Which command is executed in Huawei VRP system view to enable the Huawei Redundancy Protocol?
options: hrp enable
vrrp start
firewall cluster on
ha mode active
questions.explanation: The command `hrp enable` activates the HRP process and begins heartbeat transmission and state synchronization.

questions.stem: Which command configures a firewall interface to be monitored by VGMP so that its failure decrements the VGMP priority?
options: hrp track interface <interface-name>
interface monitor enable
vrrp track link
ha watch port
questions.explanation: In Huawei firewalls, executing `hrp track interface <interface-type> <interface-number>` registers the specified interface with VGMP for health tracking.

questions.stem: When HRP configuration synchronization is active, what prefix typically appears before the CLI command prompt on the secondary firewall?
options: [HRP_Active]
[HRP_Standby]
[Master_Node]
[Sync_Disabled]
questions.explanation: On the standby firewall, the CLI prompt is typically modified to `HRP_S` or `HRP_Standby` to indicate that local configuration is locked and synchronized from the active unit (`HRP_A` / `HRP_Active`).

questions.stem: Why does HRP lock out direct configuration changes on the Standby firewall by default?
options: To prevent conflicting configuration discrepancies between the clustered firewalls
Because the standby firewall's flash memory is physically removed
Because the standby firewall runs a different operating system
To allow unauthorized guest users to reconfigure security rules
questions.explanation: To guarantee consistent policy enforcement, configurations should only be performed on the Active firewall, which automatically replicates them to the Standby firewall. Modifying the Standby directly causes split-brain configuration mismatches.

questions.stem: Which CLI command forces an immediate manual batch synchronization of configuration from the active firewall to the standby peer?
options: hrp sync config
copy running startup
save cluster
vrrp update now
questions.explanation: Executing `hrp sync config` on the active firewall forces an immediate batch synchronization of all configuration parameters to the standby unit.

questions.stem: What is the function of the 'Preemption Mode' setting in firewall hot standby?
options: It causes the firewall to randomly reboot during network congestion
When a failed primary firewall recovers, it automatically reclaims the Active role after a configurable preemption delay
It permanently shuts down the secondary firewall
It prevents any user from accessing web services
questions.explanation: Preemption mode allows the primary firewall (with higher default priority) to reclaim the Active role once it recovers from a failure. A preemption delay is configured to allow routing protocols and interfaces to stabilize before reclaiming traffic.

questions.stem: Why is it critical to configure a 'Preemption Delay' (e.g. 60 seconds) rather than allowing immediate preemption upon primary firewall recovery?
options: To let the primary firewall's cooling fans accelerate
To allow routing protocols (OSPF/BGP), physical interfaces, and session tables to fully converge before traffic is switched back, preventing packet loss
To give the administrator time to cancel the preemption manually
Because the standby firewall requires 60 seconds to format its storage
questions.explanation: If the primary firewall preempts immediately upon booting, routing tables and neighbor adjacencies may not have converged, resulting in blackholed traffic. A delay ensures complete network stabilization before traffic switchback.

questions.stem: What occurs in a 'Split-Brain' condition when the heartbeat connection between two firewalls is completely severed while both units remain powered on?
options: Both firewalls perceive the peer as dead; both transition to the Active state, causing IP/MAC conflicts on virtual IP addresses
Both firewalls automatically enter sleep mode
The firewalls merge into a single physical unit
All network packets are converted into frame relay
questions.explanation: When heartbeat connectivity is lost, each firewall assumes the peer has failed. Both promote themselves to Active/Master, claiming the same virtual IP and virtual MAC addresses, resulting in ARP thrashing, IP conflicts, and widespread network paralysis.

questions.stem: Which command is used to check the operational status of HRP, the active/standby role, and heartbeat link health?
options: display hrp state
display vrrp brief
display ha status
display cluster info
questions.explanation: The command `display hrp state` outputs the current HRP operational state (e.g., Active or Standby), local and peer VGMP priorities, heartbeat link status, and synchronization counters.

questions.stem: Why is it recommended to configure multiple redundant heartbeat interfaces or an Eth-Trunk heartbeat between firewalls?
options: To increase the speed of user web browsing
To prevent a single cable failure from triggering a devastating Split-Brain condition
To allow the firewalls to mine cryptocurrency in idle periods
To eliminate the need for VRRP virtual IP addresses
questions.explanation: Heartbeat redundancy (via dual physical links or link aggregation) ensures that the failure of a single cable or SFP module does not sever heartbeat communications, protecting the cluster against split-brain failures.

questions.stem: How does HRP determine which firewall is Active when both firewalls are powered on simultaneously with equal initial VGMP priorities (65000)?
options: They flip a random coin electronically
They compare configured roles (e.g., `hrp standby config` or preemption settings) or use tie-breaking rules such as lower heartbeat IP or MAC address
The firewall with larger physical dimensions becomes Active
Both firewalls remain permanently disabled until manual intervention
questions.explanation: If priorities are equal, configured roles (`hrp standby config`), preemption rules, or tie-breakers (such as IP address comparison) dictate which firewall assumes the Active role.

questions.stem: Why must Server-Map tables be synchronized via HRP in addition to session tables?
options: Because Server-Map entries store user desktop wallpaper preferences
To ensure that dynamic pinholes for multi-channel protocols (e.g. FTP data) and static NAT Server mappings are immediately available on the peer during failover
Because Server-Map entries contain the firewall serial numbers
To convert public IP addresses into private IP addresses
questions.explanation: Synchronizing Server-Map entries ensures that active multi-channel data transfers (FTP, SIP) and NAT Server mappings seamlessly continue without requiring renegotiation when a failover occurs.

questions.stem: How does HRP synchronization of IPsec Security Associations (SAs) benefit remote branch VPN connections during firewall failover?
options: It requires remote branch routers to re-enter their pre-shared keys
The backup firewall assumes the existing IPsec SAs, allowing encrypted VPN tunnels to continue forwarding data without renegotiating IKE Phase 1 or Phase 2
It changes the encryption algorithm from AES to DES
It permanently disables the IPsec tunnel
questions.explanation: Replicating IPsec SAs allows the standby firewall to decrypt and encrypt ongoing IPsec traffic immediately upon taking over, avoiding tunnel renegotiation dropped packets and IKE re-authentication delays.

questions.stem: In standard VRRP, how does an interface track another interface's status?
options: vrrp vrid <id> track interface <interface-name> [reduced <value>]
interface track enable
vrrp follow port
track link status
questions.explanation: In VRRP, the command `vrrp vrid <id> track interface <interface> [reduced <value>]` dynamically decrements VRRP priority if the tracked interface goes down.

questions.stem: In Load-Balancing mode with two firewalls, why does symmetric routing engineering matter?
options: To prevent firewalls from overheating
Because stateful firewalls require session synchronization to handle return traffic if forward and return packets take different firewall paths
Because Ethernet switches cannot learn two MAC addresses simultaneously
Because routing protocols cannot run on standby firewalls
questions.explanation: Asymmetric traffic paths cause return packets to reach a firewall that did not see the initial SYN. Without quick session synchronization, the firewall drops the return packet as an invalid state transition.

questions.stem: Can HRP heartbeat communication be authenticated using a shared secret key?
options: No, HRP packets are always unauthenticated cleartext
Yes, a shared key can be configured using `hrp key <password>` to verify heartbeat packet authenticity and prevent spoofing
HRP can only be authenticated using physical iris scanners
Authentication is handled automatically by the ISP router
questions.explanation: Administrators can configure an HRP authentication key (`hrp key <key>`) to cryptographically authenticate heartbeat packets exchanged between the firewalls, preventing unauthorized injection of forged VGMP packets.

questions.stem: Can the priority deduction value applied by VGMP when an interface fails be customized?
options: No, it is permanently hardcoded to 100
Yes, administrators can specify custom priority reduction values when tracking interfaces or IP links
VGMP priority can only be modified by rebooting
Priority reduction is prohibited by RFC standards
questions.explanation: Administrators can customize the priority deduction value (e.g. `hrp track interface GigabitEthernet 0/0/1 reduced 50`) to tailor failover sensitivity across multi-interface topologies.

questions.stem: What is the fundamental difference in physical network deployment between an Intrusion Detection System (IDS) and an Intrusion Prevention System (IPS)?
options: IDS is deployed inline, whereas IPS is deployed out-of-path
IDS is deployed out-of-path (via port mirroring/TAP), whereas IPS is deployed in-line directly in the traffic forwarding path
IDS operates only over wireless networks, whereas IPS operates only over copper cabling
There is no difference in deployment; both are deployed exclusively on client desktops
questions.explanation: An IDS is deployed out-of-path (out-of-band) using switch port mirroring (SPAN) or physical TAPs to passively inspect copies of traffic. An IPS is deployed in-line directly in the live forwarding path to inspect and actively block malicious traffic in real time.

questions.stem: Why can an inline IPS actively block an exploit packet before it reaches the victim, whereas an out-of-path IDS cannot?
options: The IPS has faster electrical cables than the IDS

Because the IPS sits directly in the transmission path, it can drop malicious packets or reset connections immediately before forwarding; the IDS receives only a passive mirrored copy after the packet has already traveled to the victim
The IDS is prohibited by international standards from sending alert emails
The IPS converts all TCP packets into unencrypted UDP broadcasts
questions.explanation: Because an inline IPS sits directly in the data flow, it inspects packets before forwarding them and can immediately drop malicious packets or inject TCP resets. An out-of-path IDS receives only a mirrored copy; the original packet has already reached the target host.

questions.stem: What is the primary operational mechanism of signature-based intrusion detection in an IPS?
options: Comparing network traffic payloads and headers against a database of known attack patterns and vulnerability characteristics
Measuring ambient server room temperature fluctuations
Randomly dropping 10% of all incoming packets to deter attackers
Converting all web traffic into binary morse code
questions.explanation: Signature-based detection compares packet payloads, protocol fields, and behavioral sequences against a curated database of known vulnerability exploits and attack signatures, offering high detection accuracy and low false-positive rates for known threats.

questions.stem: What is the principal operational limitation of signature-based intrusion detection?
options: It consumes excessive electrical power
It is fundamentally incapable of detecting novel, previously unknown zero-day attacks for which no signature has been created
It can only inspect packets transmitted over dial-up modems
It permanently disables all firewall routing capabilities
questions.explanation: Signature detection relies on prior knowledge. When a completely new exploit or zero-day vulnerability emerges, no signature exists in the database, allowing the attack to bypass signature inspection undetected until a vendor signature update is released.

questions.stem: What is the major technical advantage of anomaly-based intrusion detection over signature-based detection?
options: It requires zero CPU or memory resources on the firewall
It can detect novel, unknown zero-day attacks and abnormal behavioral deviations by comparing real-time traffic against an established baseline of normal network activity
It guarantees a 0% false-positive rate under all network conditions
It eliminates the need for user passwords across the enterprise
questions.explanation: Anomaly detection constructs a mathematical profile of normal baseline behavior (bandwidth, protocol distribution, connection rates). Statistically significant deviations trigger alerts, enabling the detection of previously unseen zero-day attacks and stealthy worms.

questions.stem: What is the primary operational drawback associated with anomaly-based detection mechanisms?
options: It can only inspect ICMP echo packets
It tends to produce higher false-positive rates because legitimate but unusual business traffic spikes may be flagged as attacks
It requires physical hardware replacement every 30 days
It is incompatible with standard Ethernet frames
questions.explanation: Defining 'normal' network behavior is difficult in dynamic enterprise environments. Legitimate events (e.g., sudden software rollouts, marketing campaigns, large backups) can deviate from the baseline, generating false-positive alarms.

questions.stem: What are 'Predefined Signatures' in a Huawei USG series firewall IPS?
options: Signatures that must be written manually by the enterprise network administrator in C++
Built-in threat signatures created, tested, and regularly updated by Huawei security research teams via online intelligence updates
Signatures stored exclusively on local USB flash drives
Signatures that expire after exactly 60 seconds of use
questions.explanation: Predefined signatures are vendor-provided signatures shipped with the firewall firmware and continually updated via Huawei Security Intelligence Center online feeds to protect against emerging CVEs and exploits.

questions.stem: Under what circumstances would an enterprise administrator create 'User-Defined Signatures' on an IPS?
options: To protect proprietary internal enterprise applications or address custom threats not covered by predefined vendor signatures
Because predefined signatures cannot be used on firewalls
To format the firewall's internal solid-state storage
To disable all IP routing on the border router
questions.explanation: User-defined signatures allow security teams to create custom snort-like rules or regular expressions tailored to proprietary enterprise software, localized malware variants, or immediate hotfixes before official vendor signatures are published.

questions.stem: When a Huawei IPS signature detects an active remote code execution attack and its configured action is 'Block', what does the firewall do?
options: It logs the event but forwards the packet to the destination server
It discards the malicious packet and can optionally reset the TCP connection or blacklist the attacking source IP
It encrypts the packet and sends it to the cloud
It permanently disables the firewall's cooling fan
questions.explanation: The 'Block' action terminates the threat by dropping the malicious packet, terminating the TCP session (via TCP RST), and optionally placing the attacking source IP into a temporary blacklist to prevent subsequent connection attempts.

questions.stem: When an IPS signature's action is configured as 'Alert', how is matching traffic handled?
options: The packet is dropped and deleted immediately
The firewall generates a security event log/alarm, but allows the packet to pass through to the destination
The firewall automatically reboots into safe mode
The packet is converted into a DNS query
questions.explanation: The 'Alert' action produces an audit log entry or security alarm while permitting the traffic to proceed without interruption, commonly used during initial IPS deployment tuning to evaluate potential false positives.

questions.stem: What is the primary technical advantage of the Flow-Based (Stream-Based) antivirus scanning method utilized in Huawei USG firewalls?
options: It can inspect files larger than 100 gigabytes without using memory
It inspects data streams in real time on the fly as packets transit the firewall without caching entire files in memory, delivering high throughput and low latency
It completely replaces the need for endpoint antivirus software
It does not require virus signature database updates
questions.explanation: Flow-based antivirus scans packet streams in real time using specialized hardware and pattern matching algorithms without buffering complete multi-megabyte files in RAM, enabling multi-gigabit line-rate throughput.

questions.stem: What is a characteristic disadvantage of traditional File-Based antivirus inspection compared to Flow-Based inspection?
options: File-based inspection cannot detect known viruses
The firewall must buffer and reassemble the entire file in memory before scanning, resulting in higher memory consumption, increased latency, and potential buffer exhaustion on large files
File-based inspection operates only on wireless access points
File-based inspection is prohibited by national cybersecurity standards
questions.explanation: File-based scanning reconstructs the entire file in RAM before scanning. For multi-gigabit gateways handling millions of concurrent flows, buffering complete files introduces substantial latency and can overwhelm firewall memory buffers.

questions.stem: Which of the following application layer protocols is commonly supported for malware inspection by Huawei firewall Antivirus engines?
options: HTTP, FTP, SMTP, POP3, IMAP, and SMB
BGP, OSPF, and RIP routing updates
Ethernet CRC checksum frames
Physical Layer optical laser pulses
questions.explanation: Huawei NGFW Antivirus inspects prominent file transfer and communication protocols: Web (HTTP), File transfer (FTP, SMB), and Email (SMTP, POP3, IMAP).

questions.stem: In Huawei firewall antivirus configuration, what does the 'Declare' action signify for email protocols?
options: Deleting the recipient's entire mailbox
Permitting the email attachment to pass through while inserting a warning notification or modifying the email subject header to alert the recipient
Sending a physical letter to the sender's postal address
Disabling all incoming email for 30 days
questions.explanation: The 'Declare' action allows an infected email to be delivered but modifies the message (e.g., adding a warning banner to the subject or body, or stripping the infected attachment) to inform the user of the threat.

questions.stem: What is the primary operational objective of implementing URL Filtering on an enterprise firewall?
options: To accelerate DNS caching speed across local servers
To regulate, monitor, and restrict employee web browsing to specific categories of websites (e.g., blocking adult, gambling, or phishing sites)
To replace web servers with firewall hardware
To force all web browsers to use the same font size
questions.explanation: URL Filtering controls employee web access, preventing visits to malicious websites (phishing, malware distribution), non-work-related sites (gambling, gaming), or high-bandwidth consumption portals (video streaming).

questions.stem: What are Predefined URL Categories in Huawei USG firewalls?
options: Categories that must be typed manually by the administrator one URL at a time
A comprehensive, cloud-updated classification database (e.g., Finance, Education, Adult, Malicious) maintained by Huawei Security Intelligence
Categories stored on read-only optical discs inside the firewall chassis
Categories that only apply during nighttime hours
questions.explanation: Predefined categories group millions of global URLs into structured classifications (Business, Social, Entertainment, Security Threats). The database is dynamically updated via cloud intelligence.

questions.stem: On a Huawei firewall configured with URL Filtering, what is the evaluation priority of the URL Whitelist compared to category rules and blacklists?
options: Lowest priority; evaluated only if all other rules fail
Highest priority; if a requested URL matches the Whitelist, it is permitted immediately without checking blacklists or category rules
Equal priority; resolved by coin toss
Whitelists are evaluated only on alternate days of the week
questions.explanation: The Whitelist has the highest precedence in URL filtering. Any URL matching a whitelist entry is immediately permitted, bypassing category inspection and blacklists.

questions.stem: When a user attempts to browse a website whose domain name matches the configured URL Blacklist, what is the default result?
options: The request is permitted with high priority
The connection is blocked immediately and a block notification page is presented to the user
The user's computer monitor is turned off
The web page is translated into Latin
questions.explanation: The Blacklist has absolute blocking priority. Any request matching a blacklist pattern is blocked immediately, terminating the connection and displaying a customizable warning/block page.

questions.stem: How does Huawei NGFW File Filtering accurately identify file types even if a malicious user renames an executable file from `malware.exe` to `document.txt`?
options: By reading only the file extension characters in the file name
By analyzing the true file type through file header magic numbers and binary structural signatures, independent of the file extension
By contacting the user to ask for the genuine file type
By converting all files into PDF documents
questions.explanation: Attackers frequently rename malicious executables (`.exe`) to harmless extensions (`.txt`, `.jpg`). Huawei File Filtering inspects the binary file header magic bytes (e.g., `MZ` for PE executables, `%PDF` for PDFs) to identify the true file type.

questions.stem: What is the primary function of Content Filtering on an enterprise firewall?
options: To measure the physical length of network cables
To scan application payloads (web pages, web posts, emails) for sensitive keywords (e.g., proprietary project names, confidential data) to prevent data leakage
To format the hard drives of internal servers
To change the color scheme of corporate websites
questions.explanation: Content Filtering performs deep text analysis on transmitted data (HTTP posts, email text, search queries) to detect and block predefined sensitive keywords, preventing data exfiltration and policy violations.

questions.stem: Which of the following represents a valid severity level for an IPS signature on a Huawei firewall?
options: High, Medium, Low, and Informational
Atomic, Molecular, Cellular, and Organism
Alpha, Beta, Gamma, and Delta
Gold, Silver, Bronze, and Platinum
questions.explanation: Huawei IPS signatures are categorized by threat impact into four standardized severity ratings: High (critical exploits, RCE), Medium (privilege escalation), Low (information disclosure), and Informational (scanning, protocol anomaly).

questions.stem: Why would an administrator configure an 'Exception' within an IPS profile?
options: To permanently disable the entire IPS engine
To override the default action or severity of a specific signature (e.g., changing action from Block to Alert) without altering the global signature database
To delete the firewall operating system
To allow unauthorized users to log in as root
questions.explanation: An Exception rule allows administrators to customize the behavior of individual signatures. If a specific signature triggers false positives on an internal business application, changing its action to Alert or Pass in the Exception list prevents business interruption.

questions.stem: What does Protocol Anomaly Detection verify when inspecting network traffic?
options: It checks whether the user is wearing an official uniform
It verifies whether traffic strictly conforms to standardized RFC specifications (e.g., legal HTTP request lengths, valid header formatting, valid DNS transaction fields)
It measures the electrical resistance of the network interface
It counts the number of letters in the user's password
questions.explanation: Protocol Anomaly Detection checks incoming packets against official RFC standards, flagging malformed headers, illegal field lengths, or unexpected command sequences that indicate fuzzing, exploit payloads, or protocol abuse.

questions.stem: How is an IPS Profile activated to inspect live production traffic on a Huawei NGFW?
options: By typing `ips start` in user view
By binding the configured IPS Profile to a Security Policy rule whose action is 'Permit'
By assigning the IPS Profile to an empty USB storage port
By rebooting all connected desktop computers
questions.explanation: In Huawei NGFWs, security inspection profiles (IPS, AV, URL filtering) are applied by associating them with a 'Permit' rule in the Security Policy. Traffic matching the policy is then passed through the assigned IPS engine.

questions.stem: Why is it essential for an enterprise firewall to maintain regular, automated updates of its Antivirus signature database?
options: Because thousands of new malware variants and ransomware strains emerge daily across the global Internet
Because the firewall hardware automatically deletes all signatures every 24 hours
To prevent Ethernet cables from corroding
Because older signatures increase the weight of the firewall
questions.explanation: Cyber threat actors continuously develop new malware variants, obfuscated packers, and zero-day trojans. Without daily or real-time signature updates, the antivirus engine cannot identify the latest malicious binaries.

questions.stem: Which technique is commonly employed by Huawei firewall Mail Filtering engines to combat unsolicited commercial email (spam)?
options: RBL (Real-time Blackhole List) server IP reputation querying and keyword filtering
Disconnecting all incoming email servers permanently
Converting all incoming emails into unencrypted audio files
Requiring email senders to visit the company in person
questions.explanation: Mail filtering uses Real-time Blackhole Lists (RBL), sender IP reputation databases, SPF/DKIM verification, and body keyword analysis to classify and block spam emails before delivery.

questions.stem: How does a firewall inspect search engine queries (e.g. Google or Bing searches) when HTTPS inspection is enabled?
options: By guessing the user's thoughts
By decrypting the SSL session using SSL Decryption / SSL Proxy and inspecting the HTTP GET parameters for the search keyword string
By modifying the DNS records of all search engine companies
By physically monitoring the user's keyboard
questions.explanation: Because modern search engines use HTTPS, inspection requires an SSL Decryption Policy (SSL Proxy). The firewall decrypts the TLS session, inspects the plaintext HTTP URI parameters (e.g. `?q=keyword`), and applies content/URL policies before re-encrypting.

questions.stem: What is a 'False Positive' in the context of IPS security monitoring?
options: An attack that is correctly detected and blocked by the IPS
Legitimate, benign network traffic that is incorrectly flagged and blocked by the IPS as malicious
An attack that passes through the IPS completely undetected
A hardware power failure on the firewall chassis
questions.explanation: A False Positive occurs when benign, legitimate network traffic is erroneously classified as an attack and blocked or alerted by the IPS, potentially disrupting normal business applications.

questions.stem: What is a 'False Negative' in IPS operational terminology?
options: Benign traffic that is allowed to pass normally
A real, malicious attack that the IPS fails to detect and allows to pass through to the target
An attack that triggers an alarm on all enterprise monitors
A software update that installs successfully
questions.explanation: A False Negative occurs when a genuine malicious exploit slips through the IPS completely undetected, often due to missing signatures, evasion techniques, or zero-day vulnerabilities.

questions.stem: Why is Flow-Based antivirus particularly advantageous on border firewalls handling heavy user downloads?
options: It requires zero megabytes of storage on user PCs
It avoids holding multi-megabyte files in firewall RAM buffers, preserving system memory and ensuring consistent forwarding latency during large file transfers
It allows the firewall to mine Bitcoin during quiet periods
It doubles the physical speed of the fiber optic link
questions.explanation: Flow-based scanning examines packet streams on the fly without holding whole files in memory, avoiding memory exhaustion and high latency when hundreds of concurrent users download large files.

questions.stem: What occurs when a URL Filtering rule action is set to 'Force Redirect'?
options: The user is redirected to a different specified URL (such as a corporate policy reminder page or secondary proxy)
The user's computer is rebooted into safe mode
The user is disconnected from the local network permanently
The web server is powered off
questions.explanation: Force Redirect intercepts the user's HTTP request and returns an HTTP 302 redirect response pointing the browser to a designated warning page, compliance portal, or corporate intranet URL.

questions.stem: In Huawei firewall configuration, can File Filtering rules be configured with directional granularity?
options: No, File Filtering applies identically in all directions without distinction
Yes, File Filtering can be configured specifically for Uploads (outbound data loss prevention) or Downloads (inbound malware prevention)
File Filtering works only for internal server backups
Direction is determined by the physical tilt of the firewall rack
questions.explanation: File filtering can be applied directionally: inspecting Inbound downloads (blocking executable downloads or malicious PDFs) and Outbound uploads (preventing proprietary document exfiltration).

questions.stem: How do attackers attempt to evade simple signature matching using IP packet fragmentation?
options: By splitting the malicious exploit string across multiple small IP fragments so that neither fragment alone contains the full recognizable signature pattern
By setting the IP TTL to 255
By using wireless transmission instead of copper
By deleting the IP checksum
questions.explanation: Attackers fragment packets so that exploit strings (e.g. `/bin/sh`) are split across separate fragment boundaries. To prevent evasion, modern NGFWs reassemble IP fragments before performing deep packet signature inspection.
